items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Like when I was coming up -- a lot of guys used to laugh at Clyde McCoy. He was playing "Sugar Blues" but nobody could play it like him.

ctx.x: I'd rather just be a mediocre originator. Than to be a perfect imitator. Because I don't care how well you imitate the other person, there's somebody who's going to say, 'he's copying.' He's copying. Because when you do your thing, I don't care how sad it is, you're the only one can do it. One of these days you'll be recognized, if you don't change, because

it's original, you know. Like when I was coming up -- a lot of guys used to laugh at Clyde McCoy. He was playing "Sugar Blues" but nobody could play it like him. Nobody could play it like Clyde McCoy. And he acquired immense fortune playing "Sugar Blues."
